title: Science for Grown-Ups
intro: Physics, chemistry, biology and astronomy at expert level. Time to see how much science really stuck.

questions.prompt: Which element has the chemical symbol W?
questions.explanation: W comes from wolfram, the element's older German-derived name. Tungsten has the highest melting point of any metal.

questions.prompt: Which is the only metal that is liquid at normal room temperature and pressure?
questions.explanation: Mercury melts at about −39 °C. Gallium and caesium melt just above room temperature, and bromine is liquid but is not a metal.

questions.prompt: Which element has the highest electronegativity of all, meaning it attracts bonding electrons most strongly?
questions.explanation: Fluorine tops the Pauling electronegativity scale at about 4.0, which makes it the most reactive of all the non-metals.

questions.prompt: What is the SI unit of electrical resistance?
questions.explanation: Resistance is measured in ohms, named after the German physicist Georg Simon Ohm. The siemens measures conductance, its opposite.

questions.prompt: Which cell structure is the site where proteins are built?
questions.explanation: Ribosomes read messenger RNA and join amino acids together in the right order to build proteins.

questions.prompt: In DNA, the base adenine always pairs with which other base?
questions.explanation: Adenine pairs with thymine and guanine pairs with cytosine. In RNA, uracil takes the place of thymine.

questions.prompt: What is the boundary around a black hole beyond which nothing, not even light, can escape?
questions.explanation: Once anything crosses the event horizon, escaping would need a speed greater than light, which is impossible.

questions.prompt: Titan, the only moon in the solar system with a thick atmosphere, orbits which planet?
questions.explanation: Titan is Saturn's largest moon. Its dense nitrogen atmosphere hides lakes of liquid methane and ethane.

questions.prompt: Which physicist is famous for the uncertainty principle?
questions.explanation: Heisenberg showed in 1927 that a particle's position and momentum cannot both be known exactly at the same time.

questions.prompt: Which noble gas makes up the largest share of Earth's atmosphere?
questions.explanation: Argon makes up just under 1% of the air, far more than all the other noble gases put together.

questions.prompt: Which cells in the pancreas produce insulin?
questions.explanation: Beta cells in the islets of Langerhans release insulin to lower blood sugar. Alpha cells make glucagon, which raises it.

questions.prompt: Which gas law says that, at constant temperature, the pressure of a fixed mass of gas is inversely proportional to its volume?
questions.explanation: Robert Boyle described the rule in 1662: squeeze a gas into half the space and its pressure doubles.

questions.prompt: Which type of cell division produces four genetically different sex cells?
questions.explanation: Meiosis halves the chromosome number and shuffles genes, so each egg or sperm cell is unique. Mitosis makes identical copies.

questions.prompt: Apart from the Sun, which is the brightest star in the night sky?
questions.explanation: Sirius, the Dog Star, is bright because it is both luminous and close, about 8.6 light-years away.

questions.prompt: Which type of bond holds the two strands of the DNA double helix together?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen bonds between paired bases are weak enough to let the strands unzip when DNA is copied.

questions.prompt: Which particle carries the electromagnetic force?
questions.explanation: Photons are particles of light and carry the electromagnetic force. Gluons carry the strong force and W bosons the weak force.

questions.prompt: Which mineral is number 1, the softest, on the Mohs hardness scale?
questions.explanation: Talc is so soft you can scratch it with a fingernail. Gypsum is 2, calcite 3 and quartz 7.

questions.prompt: Which scientist first proposed continental drift, the idea that the continents slowly move?
questions.explanation: Wegener set out the idea in 1912. It was widely rejected until plate tectonics explained how continents move.

questions.prompt: Which vitamin is mainly needed for blood clotting?
questions.explanation: Vitamin K helps the liver make clotting proteins. Newborn babies are often given it for this reason.

questions.prompt: Which is the nearest large spiral galaxy to the Milky Way?
questions.explanation: The Andromeda Galaxy is about 2.5 million light-years away and is one of the farthest things visible with the naked eye.

questions.prompt: What is it called when a solid turns straight into a gas without melting first, as dry ice does?
questions.explanation: Dry ice is frozen carbon dioxide. At normal air pressure it skips the liquid stage and sublimes straight into gas.

questions.prompt: Which chemist published a periodic table in 1869 that left gaps for elements not yet discovered?
questions.explanation: Mendeleev predicted the properties of missing elements such as gallium and germanium, which were later found to match.

questions.prompt: Sound travels faster through water than through air.
questions.explanation: Sound moves at about 1,500 metres per second in water, more than four times faster than in air, because the particles are closer together.

questions.prompt: Venus spins in the opposite direction to most planets, so on Venus the Sun rises in the west.
questions.explanation: Venus has a backwards, very slow spin. One Venus day is longer than its year.

questions.prompt: Mitochondria contain their own DNA, separate from the DNA in the nucleus.
questions.explanation: Mitochondria have their own small loop of DNA, a clue that they were once free-living bacteria.

questions.prompt: Bats are the only mammals capable of true powered flight.
questions.explanation: Flying squirrels and colugos glide, but only bats flap their wings to fly.

questions.prompt: An electron has more mass than a proton.
questions.explanation: A proton is about 1,836 times heavier than an electron, which is why almost all of an atom's mass is in its nucleus.

questions.prompt: What is the atomic number of iron?
questions.explanation: Iron has 26 protons in its nucleus, so its atomic number is 26. Its symbol, Fe, comes from the Latin ferrum.

questions.prompt: Absolute zero is 0 kelvin. What is it in degrees Celsius, to the nearest whole degree?
questions.explanation: Absolute zero is −273.15 °C, the coldest temperature possible, where particles have the least possible energy.

questions.prompt: To the nearest minute, about how long does sunlight take to reach Earth?
questions.explanation: Light covers the 150 million kilometres from the Sun in about 8 minutes 20 seconds.
